claim: import assigns ids by position to rows without one: a finding inserted above the numbered rows takes an id that already exists, and both records keep it with no way back through the tool

Exit 1 reads as "the state is red", not as "your definition is malformed".

claim: stale_tree returns None without refs/remotes/origin/HEAD and says nothing, so the freshness gate is silently inert for a checkout with no remote or with a remote not named origin

The hunter's CI example is wrong on current git: `git remote add origin` + `fetch` does create origin/HEAD, so the residue is no-remote and non-origin checkouts.

root: a gate that cannot go red

claim: run-role.sh writes the spend line to the journal whatever the run's exit code, so a run cut off by --max-turns is recorded as an ordinary completed run

The journal is the only memory the next session has, and it now says the block was hunted, with no word that the assignment was truncated. In a project with Cyrillic file names those paths never match `owned` (which comes from ls-files -z) and are invisible to coupling altogether, so a seam between two blocks cannot be reported at all.
invariant: 5 (git is the source of file truth; paths are handled NUL-separated)
root: git output parsed as plain text, without -z / quotePath

claim: The named-files gate is a plain substring test, so a longer path that contains an owned path satisfies the gate for both: a report naming src/api.ts.snap marks src/api.ts as named

Any file whose path is a prefix of a sibling's — a snapshot, a .map, a .test.ts next to a .ts, an index.ts under a longer directory — is closed by naming the sibling. The gate was built to stop the "read 25 of 25" claim, and this is the cheapest way past it that does not even require intent.

claim: On a history of 20 commits or fewer mass_cutoff equals the largest commit, so no mass commit is ever skipped and the initial whole-tree commit pairs every file with every other
scenario: Run over synthetic histories of sizes 1..100: for n ≤ 20 the cutoff equals the largest commit (12 → 12, 19 → 19, 20 → 20) and the guard is a strict `>`, so nothing is skipped; from 21 on it starts to bite (21 → 20, 100 → 96). On a young repository `coupling` therefore treats the initial commit containing the whole tree as an ordinary change, and three formatting sweeps reach together ≥ 3: the output is a wall of pairs that say nothing about a seam, while order's churn counts every block as touched by every sweep. The threshold comment promises exactly the opposite protection, and a new repository is when coupling is run.
invariant: 8 (a number must hold where it is applied)
root: threshold that does not hold at the edge of its range

claim: summary --aged slices its machine block with text.index(' -->') and json.loads: a block title or path containing ' -->' gives a traceback instead of the drift table

A title ending in '-->' fails the same way. claim: Without a result event axes.py reports turns None, cost $0.00 and an output count its own comment calls a stream artefact, in the format of a real measurement; a truncated last line raises

The same stream with the result event removed — what a killed or capped run leaves: "spend: 0 min, None turns, … output 0k, cost estimate $0.00", exit 0, and run-role.sh writes that to the journal, recording an expensive truncated run as free. The same stream with its last line cut short: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, exit 1 — under `set -e` in run-role.sh that costs the journal line, the agent's reply and the run's exit code.

claim: init rewrites updated_at on every run, so a no-op re-run always dirties state.json
scenario: Reproduced: two consecutive `init` runs on an unchanged definition differ only in updated_at (2026-09-24T14:50:59Z → …T14:51:00Z); every other key is identical. CI that runs `review.py init && review.py coverage --no-write && review.py check` and then asserts a clean working tree — the usual shape for a generated-artifact gate — fails on a correct state, and the honest workaround is to stop running init in CI, which is what the gate existed to guarantee.

claim: The verifier's coverage-verdict gate matches the bare word 'complete' anywhere in the report, so 'I completed the check' satisfies a gate meant to demand a statement about what was left unreviewed

COVERAGE_VERDICT matches "complete" inside "completed", so a verb about verdicts answers the question about coverage — the very distinction the neighbouring hunter gate is strict about. The Russian half fails the other way: "Проверка завершена полностью" and "все находки проверены" match nothing, so an honest ru report is rejected.

claim: Four thresholds carry no measurement or reference: REF_LIST_LIMIT=80, the 200-character 'manifest nearly empty' bound, CLAIM_MAX=220 / SCENARIO_MAX=700 and COUPLING_HUB_BLOCKS=6
scenario: Read against every other constant in the file, each of which carries its source (READABLE_LINES 6000 from measured runs and the MSR 2022 study, STALE_TREE_DAYS 7 from the twelve-day incident, ROOT_RULE_AT 3 from variant analysis, COUPLING_MIN_TOGETHER/MIN_SHARE from the first project and Zimmermann et al.). A project whose manifests are terse fails "manifest is empty or nearly empty" at 199 characters and nothing in the file says whether 200 is defensible; the same question about 80 reference files or 6 hub blocks cannot be answered by reading. Tuning them becomes taste, and the next constant added follows the precedent of the bare ones.

root: threshold without its source

scenario: Reproduced: a manifest paragraph reading "The template uses {{HUNTER_NOTE}} and {{FILES}} as placeholders" makes `prompt H1 --role hunter` exit 2 with "template hunter.md has substitutions left without a value: {{HUNTER_NOTE}}" — hunter.md contains no such placeholder and the author edits the wrong file. claim: One marker exempts every hit in the window below it, not just the call it was written above — the exact failure guard-grep.sh was written to replace grep -B with
scenario: Reproduced: a file with `// outbox-allowed:` on line 2 and broker.Publish( on lines 3, 4, 5 and 6 (default window 3) reports only line 6 — one escape hatch silently exempted three calls. The header states the opposite as the script's whole reason to exist: "grep runs consecutive hits together into ONE block … a marker granted to the first call silently exempts the second one three lines below it" and "here each hit is paired with the marker by LINE NUMBER … so a marker covers exactly the call it was written above and nothing else". The rewrite reproduces the defect it names, so a gate adopted on that promise lets through every forbidden call within three lines of an existing hatch.

claim: listed() runs git ls-files with check=True, so a pathspec in blocks.json that git rejects makes check and coverage die with a CalledProcessError traceback instead of naming the bad pattern
scenario: Reproduced: a paths entry of ":(nosuchmagic)src" — a typo in the pathspec magic the kit invites projects to use for exclusions — makes `check` exit 1 with subprocess.CalledProcessError on `git ls-files --stage -z -- :(nosuchmagic)src`, and `coverage` exit 1 the same way, while `status` exits 0 because it never expands the pattern. git's own message ("Invalid pathspec magic") is swallowed, so the user sees a Python stack trace and an exit code that reads as "the state is red". The neighbouring gate at 2458 handles a pattern that matches nothing; a pattern git refuses to parse has no handler.
invariant: 12 (a traceback reachable from a legal command line); 3 (a refusal names the command that fixes it)

claim: The cited-line gate is guarded by isinstance(line, int), so a finding whose line is written as a string skips the check entirely while findings.md still renders it as a real location
scenario: Reproduced: two identical open findings on a 3-line file, one with "line": 9999 and one with "line": "9999". check reports only the first ("line 9999 is cited, but src/api.ts has 3") and says nothing about the second, yet findings.md renders both as `src/api.ts:9999`. The gate is described in its own comment as "the cheapest sign of fabrication"; a draft findings file is hand-written JSONL, where a quoted number is an ordinary slip, and import copies the field through untouched.
invariant: 1 (the gate must not be silently skippable); 12 (a field outside its type is a refusal, not a pass)
root: report parser matches shape, not meaning

claim: [R1-001, fix review round 1] The new guard for "a gate that cannot go red" does not see a gate whose message is not a literal
scenario: run against a copy of the kit. Adding to `cmd_check` ```python if st.get("review_id") != defn.get("review_id"): msg = f"review_id mismatch" problems.append(msg) ``` — a gate with no test at all — leaves `GateRegistryTest` green (rc 0) and the whole suite green (205 tests, OK). The same holds for `problems.append(dup_problem(...))`. Written with a literal message instead, the identical gate turns `GateRegistryTest` red. So the guard covers one of the two shapes the tool actually uses, and the shape it misses is the one three existing gates are written in — the next gate added by copying its neighbour is untested and nothing says so.

claim: [R1-002, fix review round 1] `summary --aged` now counts one file under two names — the opposite of what the change claims
scenario: reproduced end to end. A repository whose base commit is followed by two commits — one touching `src/a.ts` and `src/b.ts`, one touching `src/b.ts` — gives `summary --aged`: ``` HEAD: H1 commits: 2 files: 3 <- two files exist dev: H1 commits: 2 files: 2 <- correct ``` The same run against `dev`'s `review.py` prints 2. Every file that is first in one commit and not first in another is counted twice, so the drift table over-reports on any real history, in the one file that is meant to outlive `docs/review/`.

claim: [R1-003, fix review round 1] The named-files gate now refuses a report that writes `./src/api.ts`
scenario: reproduced end to end. A block owning `src/api.ts` and `src/util.ts`, with a hunter report whose coverage list is ``` - ./src/api.ts - ./src/util.ts ``` gives `check` exit 1: "H1: 2 of 2 block files are not named by full path in any report (src/api.ts, src/util.ts)". The same report passes on `dev`. The report is honest and complete; the gate refuses it, and the author's only repair is to rewrite the paths.

claim: [R1-004, fix review round 1] A quoted verdict still closes a hypothesis when it is quoted by indentation or by `>`
scenario: run on the parser, block id `T1`: | report body | verdicts read | |---|---| | ` ```markdown ` … `- T1.1 — checked: <what proves it>` … ` ``` ` | `{}` — fixed | | a four-space indented block holding the same line | `{'T1.1': ['checked']}` | | `> - T1.1 — checked: <what proves it>` | `{'T1.1': ['checked']}` | | `<!-- - T1.1 — checked: … -->` | `{'T1.1': ['checked']}` | A report that restates its assignment as an indented example, or quotes the template with `>`, closes its hypotheses without answering them and `check` prints "review state is consistent" — the same false pass T1-001 describes, through a neighbouring door.

claim: [R1-005, fix review round 1] `axes.py` changed which `result` event it measures, and this is in no report and under no test
scenario: a stream carrying a 40-turn `success` result and a 2-turn `error_max_turns` result reports, in either order, `spend: 10 min, 40 turns … $5.00` with no outcome word — the cut-off marker in the shorter event is dropped. In the same round the kit's own journal gained `spend: 0 min, 2 turns, 329 tool calls … cost estimate $67.92` — a line that reads as a measurement and cannot be one — and neither `axes.py` nor the guards added beside it say so.

claim: [R1-006, fix review round 1] The changelog's Breaking section holds five fixes that are not breaking, and not the change that is

claim: [R1-007, fix review round 1] Two new rules in the fix role template, recorded nowhere
scenario: a later editor reworks `references/fix.md` — the file is T2's subject and T2 has not run yet — and drops either rule. scenario: cmd_setup selects the entry point by language at review.py:3486 and then hardcodes English names at lines 3509, 3511, 3513 and 3516. Run against an empty repository, `setup --project Проект --lang ru` writes a Russian blocks.json, a Russian invariants skeleton and a Russian docs/review/README.md, then prints a checklist pointing at invariants.example.md, blocks.example.json, manifest.example.md and agent-banner.md. A scan of every tracked file finds the four Russian samples named nowhere in the kit: they ship and the user has no way to discover them.
invariant: the bilingual contract; the entry point in the same function proves the selection was intended
root: the Russian half of the bilingual assets is unwired

claim: The entry point that setup copies into every project as docs/review/README.md is behind the tool: no fixreview role or report name, no fix gate, no import --append, and its prompts/ list omits fixreview.md
scenario: A lead session that knows nothing does what the file promises — one command and the full picture. It runs the diff review as step 8 describes, writes the report under a name of its own, then `set-status <ID> closed`; check answers 'closed with fixed findings, but there is no fix reviewer report', because the gate globs <ID>-<slug>.fixreview-*.md. Earlier, moving the next block to running, it meets a fix-gate refusal the entry point never warned it about. Neither file contains the strings fixreview, fix_gate, --append, restamp or backfill. Same in entry-point.ru.md.
invariant: invariant 9 applied to the scaffold the project actually reads
root: the fix and fix-review round mechanism is not carried into the kit's documents

claim: The fix reviewer is handed a diff of any size with no statement of that size and no mention of --scope, while the hunter's prompt carries a measured reading budget
scenario: The kit's own T1 round-1 diff was 193 KB. A lead runs `prompt <ID> --role fixreview --diff main...HEAD` on a range of that size. diff_text prepends --stat and pastes the whole range; rule 1 says 'the diff is pasted below in full — read it' with no condition, and nothing states the volume, the token order of magnitude or where the budget line runs — all of which volume_note states for the hunter's file list. {{VOLUME}} occurs only in the two hunter templates, and neither fix-review template names --scope. The agent reads what fits and reports on the whole diff.
invariant: the budget must stand in the assignment, not in the lead session's head (the reasoning volume_note was written on)

claim: Lesson 13 requires every deferred finding to be fixed or rejected before the review ends, while the tool and SKILL.md treat a deferred finding with a reason as an accepted risk that ships in the summary
scenario: A lead reads the lessons before the first block, as SKILL.md:161-162 instructs, and holds the review open at the end to resolve a dozen deferred findings that render_summary writes under 'Accepted risks (deferred with a reason)' and that the completion conditions of SKILL.md:143 and entry-point.md:69-70 do not mention at all; check demands only the reason, never the resolution. Read in the other order, the same lead treats the summary's accepted-risks section as a defect. Two documents of the kit give opposite answers to 'is the review finished'. Same in lessons.ru.md:53-55.
invariant: lesson 36 of the same file — a lesson that does not reach the rules is worse than no lesson

claim: The Makefile snippet defines no generic `review` target, while SKILL.md offers `make review` as an example value for the cli field that every hint is built from
scenario: A project pastes makefile-snippet.mk into its Makefile and, following SKILL.md:28-30, sets "cli": "make review" in blocks.json. project_cli then builds every hint and refusal from that string: `make review init`, `make review coverage`, `make review restamp H1`. Run against the shipped snippet, `make review init` answers 'No rule to make target review' and exits 2, because the snippet defines only review-init, review-status and the rest. The package.json snippet does define the generic target, which is why `npm run review --` works.
invariant: hints are assembled from CLI, and the shipped snippets must agree with what SKILL.md says cli may hold
root: shipped assets hardcode `make` as the project's CLI

claim: The toy's findings.md header holds the literal `<skill>` path while its blocks.json sets no `cli`, so the file can never equal the regenerated one and check is red in every copy of the example
scenario: render_findings_md writes the 'GENERATED by' header from CLI, which without a `cli` field in blocks.json is python3 plus the tool's real absolute path. The shipped file carries the placeholder `python3 <skill>/scripts/review.py`, which the tool never produces, so the by-content comparison at review.py:3106 can never succeed. Copy examples/toy into a fresh repository and run check, as its README instructs: it exits 1 with 'findings.md diverged from findings.jsonl' on top of the unowned README.md. Adding a matching `cli` field, together with that exclusion, makes check exit 0.
invariant: the reference example of a green review must be green
root: the kit's own gates are never run over examples/toy

claim: `roots`, the class view the three-instance guard gate rests on, is named by no message of the tool, by no line of SKILL.md and by no line of the entry point, so a lead cannot learn it exists
scenario: Of the 23 subcommands, four are absent from SKILL.md: hypotheses, refs, roots and version. The entry point installed by setup names hypotheses and version, and a check warning names refs; roots is in none of the three. A lead meets 'root X: 3 instances (…) and no guard' and wants the class before choosing a guard, but the refusal names only set-finding --rule and the first four ids, and the two documents it has say nothing. It reads the register by hand or records a guard on a partial list.
invariant: hypothesis 7 — every user-facing command is in SKILL.md or reachable from it
root: the defect-class mechanism is announced in no document an agent or a lead reads

claim: Both banner assets hardcode `make review-status` with no {{CLI}} placeholder, and setup substitutes nothing in them, so a project without a Makefile pastes a dead command into every session
scenario: A Go or Rust project with no Makefile runs setup and follows step 5 of its checklist, which only prints the path to agent-banner.md. The banner says to run `make review-status`. Pasted into the root instructions file, it tells every future session of that project to run a command that does not exist — in the one document whose purpose is to stop a session from starting a parallel review. The sibling asset entry-point.md carries {{CLI}} and is substituted at review.py:3488, so the mechanism exists and this file does not use it; the kit's own AGENTS.md banner names the real path instead.
invariant: rule 5 of AGENTS.md — hints are assembled from CLI, no `make review-check` in strings
root: shipped assets hardcode `make` as the project's CLI

claim: Five cmd_check gates moved from problems to warnings leave all 248 tests green: check exits 0 on the state it refused, because GATES keys a gate by its message and those gate tests never assert the exit code
scenario: Measured against a green 248-test baseline: the block-status vocabulary gate (review.py:2876), the empty-manifest gate (2907), the phase-order gate (2885), the 'pattern matches no file' gate (3122) and the three-instances-no-guard root gate (3315) were each turned from problems.append into warnings.append in a separate copy of the kit. Every copy stayed green. check then prints the same sentence and exits 0 on the wrong state, while the registry still reports 64 of 64 gates held. _check_gates does compute which list a gate appends to, but the key drops it, and the tests at 1613, 1622, 2056, 1824 and 1700 assert only assertIn on the message.
invariant: invariant 1 and SECURITY.md: any way to make check pass on a state that is wrong is the most serious class here; invariant 12: exit codes mean something
root: a gate whose test asserts its message, not its verdict

claim: _check_gates matches only `problems.append(x)` on a Name, so a gate written with `+=` or `extend` yields no key, needs no GATES entry and no test, and the registry stays green
scenario: Measured: a new gate added to cmd_check as `problems += [f"{bid}: role `__never__` is reserved"]` left all 248 tests green, and so did the same gate written `problems.extend([...])`. The control — the identical gate written `problems.append(...)` — was killed by test_каждые_ворота_check_записаны_вместе_со_своим_тестом, which proves the guard sees exactly one spelling. Splitting a 500-line cmd_check with extend, the obvious refactor, therefore drops gates out of the registry silently, and each one can then be removed with the suite green.
invariant: invariant 2: every check comes with a test, and the test is proven by a mutation
root: class guard keyed on incidental syntax

claim: GateRegistryTest checks only that the test named beside a gate exists; nothing ties the two, so a gate registered against any existing test name satisfies the guard with zero coverage
scenario: Measured: the GATES entry for ': no manifest' was re-pointed from test_манифест_пропал_а_блок_в_работе to the unrelated test_описание_в_пределах, and all 248 tests stayed green. So the cheapest way to green after adding a gate — copy a neighbouring line's test name — passes both registry tests: the counter test compares keys against the source, and test_каждый_названный_тест_существует only looks the name up in globals(). The register then records the gate as held while silencing it changes nothing in the suite.
invariant: SECURITY.md: a check that goes green on a state that is wrong
root: guard enumerates its subject without exercising it

claim: backfill runs once in the whole suite and set-finding over several ids only on the happy path, so neither backfill's idempotence nor set-finding's all-or-nothing is held by a test
scenario: Two measured survivors. Deleting `if not stamped_blocks and not stamped_findings: return 0` from cmd_backfill (review.py:2478) left all 248 tests green: every re-run then rewrites state.json and appends another journal line, and the CI gate of the documented shape — regenerate, then require a clean tree — would go red on a correct state. Moving the register write inside cmd_set_finding's loop over ids also left the suite green: `set-finding H1-001 H1-999 deferred --reason x` would then leave H1-001 written and H1-999 refused, and no test passes an unknown id among several.
invariant: invariant 11: init, coverage, findings, backfill, restamp re-run without changing a correct state; set-finding on several ids is all-or-nothing
root: a gate that cannot go red

claim: The no-traceback class guard passes one fixed argv to every subcommand; argparse rejects it for 20 of the 23, so their bodies never run and the guard proves nothing about them
scenario: Measured by running the guard's own loop: of the 23 names it takes from --help, only set-status, set-finding and log reach a cmd_* body; the other 20 exit 2 with 'unrecognized arguments' before the command starts, so the guard asserts the absence of a traceback from argparse's own usage error. Its docstring promises that a new command falls under the rule without editing the test, and any new command with fewer than two positionals will not. The class is partly held elsewhere — check_definition validates the definition centrally, and test_блок_без_обязательного_поля_называет_поле covers status, check, order and summary — so what is broken is the guard's promise.
invariant: invariant 12: a traceback reaching the user is a defect regardless of the cause
root: guard enumerates its subject without exercising it

claim: Nothing compares the key sets of MSG['en'] and MSG['ru'], so deleting a translation leaves the suite green while T() raises KeyError at run time on the path that needs it
scenario: Measured: deleting MSG['ru']['refs_cut'] left all 248 tests green, because no test gives a block more than REF_LIST_LIMIT=80 ref_paths and render_refs never takes that branch. A Russian-language project whose block has 81 context files would then get KeyError: 'refs_cut' and a traceback out of `review prompt`, the command that hands an agent its assignment. The tables are in sync today — measured directly, both hold the same 58 keys — so this is a missing guard rather than a live defect; vol_more, sum_seams and f_invariant sit on equally unreached paths.
invariant: invariants: a string that exists in one language and not the other is a defect — T() raises KeyError at run time, not at import

claim: Mechanisms outside cmd_check that no test reaches: import's claim cap, block_risk's refusal, review_lang's fallback and cmd_next — each removable with the whole suite green
scenario: Four measured survivors. Dropping claim from import's limit loop (review.py:1888) lets a 300-character claim through import and makes check red for ever — the defect R5-005 already recorded. Dropping block_risk's die (review.py:1206) sends an invalid risk to SEVERITIES.index as a ValueError traceback out of `order`. Dropping review_lang's `if lang in LANGS` (review.py:253) turns a hand-written lang like ru-RU into a KeyError, and no gate in check validates the field. cmd_next raises unconditionally and nothing notices. Four further mechanisms the same finding names (restamp on a vanished file, coupling's share filters, inventory --under, guard-grep's --exclude) were not individually mutated.
invariant: CONTRIBUTING: every new check comes with a test, and the test is proven by mutation
root: a gate that cannot go red

claim: The space-path test asserts only that check does NOT print 'does not touch' and never checks its fixture reached that state, so silencing the gate for paths with a space leaves the suite green
scenario: Measured: adding `and " " not in f["file"]` to the commit-touches gate (review.py:3016) silences it for exactly the case test_путь_с_пробелом_не_ломает_проверку_коммита is named for, and all 248 tests stay green. Stand.commit and Stand.git call git with check=False (51, 60), so a fixture that never reaches the state is silent, and the neighbouring Cyrillic test at 2841 shows the fix — it asserts set-finding's return code. Three sibling tests the hunter accused of the same shape were cleared by mutation: breaking their mechanisms reddens the tests at 496, 1743 and 1760.
invariant: T3 manifest: a test that is green for the wrong reason, or cannot fail, is a finding
root: gate proven only by the absence of a message

claim: Only Stand.run pins a UTF-8 locale; _run_role and the bare python3 calls inherit it, so the suite's verdict rests on CPython auto-enabling UTF-8 mode in the C locale
scenario: Measured matrix: `LANG=C LC_ALL=C` is green, because CPython turns UTF-8 mode on in the C locale (the child reports utf-8, utf8_mode=1). With that safety net off — PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 — the same suite is red at 15 failures and 195 errors of 248, the first traceback being UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec from cmd_prompt's print(body) reached through run-role.sh, which inherits the environment at line 3477. _axes (3347) and the five bare python3 calls inherit it too. CI pins the git identity and the default branch but not the locale (.github/workflows/tests.yml:18).
invariant: CONTRIBUTING: the suite is the gate — a gate whose verdict depends on the machine proves nothing

claim: The Stand repositories set only user.name and user.email locally, so the developer's global git config — ignore file, commit.gpgsign — decides whether the suite passes
scenario: Both predicted cells reproduce. A global core.excludesFile holding `vendor/` reddens exactly test_шаблон_по_нетрекнутым_файлам_зовёт_git_add and nothing else: check prints 'matches no file' instead of 'matches only untracked files (1)'. A global commit.gpgsign=true reddens six tests — the three coupling tests, test_order_ставит_часто_меняющийся_блок_выше_при_равном_риске, test_origin_по_прежнему_ловит_отставание and test_setup_предупреждает_про_байткод — because Stand.commit calls git with check=False, so every failed commit is silent and no message names the cause. GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null in Stand.git removes the dependency.

claim: The claude stub emits no result event, so all six run-role.sh tests exercise the NO RESULT EVENT branch and the test named 'a successful run is written as an ordinary line' accepts that as one
scenario: Measured by running run-role.sh against the suite's own stub with exit 0: the journal line is `hunter — NO RESULT EVENT — the run was killed or the stream is truncated · spend: ? min, ? turns, 0 tool calls, … cost estimate unknown`. test_успешный_прогон_записан_обычной_строкой (3546) asserts only 'hunter — ' and the absence of RUN FAILED, so it passes on that line, and the shape of a completed spend line — the one an operator reads as 'the block was hunted' — is produced by no test of run-role.sh. test_ответ_агента_печатается_из_целого_потока asserts the reply is absent and then checks it through axes.py on a hand-written file.

claim: The NUL-path class guard inspects only list literals holding both 'git' and a name-asking flag, so splitting the repeated git prefix out of the literal blinds it and -z can be dropped unnoticed
scenario: Measured: rewriting untracked_files as `["git", "-C", str(ROOT)] + ["ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "--", *specs]` with -z dropped and splitlines() in place of split("\0") left all 248 tests green, and test_список_путей_у_git_всегда_запрашивается_NUL_разделённым never saw it, because neither literal now holds both 'git' and a flag from its list. A non-ASCII untracked path then arrives C-quoted and matches nothing. review_refs (review.py:1436) already passes the guard today: it runs `git grep -n --full-name` without -z and splits with splitlines() — read in the source, not reproduced with a fixture.
invariant: invariant 5: git is the source of file truth, paths are handled NUL-separated
root: class guard keyed on incidental syntax

claim: No fixture path contains a bracket, so the :(literal) prefix in file_sha — there because git-pathspec reads [handle] as a character class — can be deleted with the suite green
scenario: Measured: replacing file_sha's `index_rows([f":(literal){rel}"])` with `index_rows([rel])` (review.py:387) left all 248 tests green. A Next.js tree, the kit's stated target, owns app/[id]/page.tsx; with that file live in the index but not laid out on disk — a sparse checkout, or deleted without committing — the pathspec matches nothing, file_sha returns None, the block fingerprint silently loses the file and 'block files changed after the review' can never fire for it. Every path in the suite is plain ASCII, a space or Cyrillic. rule_problem and --fixed-in pass a name to git_files as a pathspec too, equally untested.
invariant: invariant 5: patterns go through git-pathspec — a [ is a character class

claim: The threshold guard walks only module-level `NAME = <number>`, so a bare threshold written as a BinOp or as a tuple assignment carries no source and the suite stays green
scenario: Measured: adding `FOO_LIMIT = 6 * 7` and `BAR_MAX, BAZ_MAX = 12, 34` at module level in review.py, with no comment above either, left all 248 tests green. test_каждое_число_в_коде_названо_и_объяснено inspects only ast.Assign nodes in the module body whose value is an ast.Constant and whose single target is an upper-case ast.Name, so `6 * 1000` — the natural way to write a derived limit — and a pair of limits introduced together both walk past it. Invariant 8 is therefore held for one spelling of an assignment only, and the next threshold added the other way carries no measurement.
invariant: invariant 8: every number has its source next to it
root: class guard keyed on incidental syntax

claim: The suite spawns the tool as PATH `python3` in seven places while using sys.executable in five, so running it under another interpreter does not test that interpreter
scenario: Stand.run calls ["python3", str(self.tool), *args], and six more sites do the same (1936, 1946, 1950, 2402, 2422, 2436), while axes.py and run-role.sh's REVIEW use sys.executable. `python3.12 -m unittest discover -s tests` would therefore report 248 tests on 3.12 while every invocation of the tool still ran on PATH python3 — a cell that measures nothing, and a version-specific defect stays invisible; the ast.unparse quote style that reddened the registry in CI, recorded at line 3932, is the precedent. Measured here: PATH python3 and sys.executable are the same 3.14.7 binary and no second interpreter exists, so the matrix cell cannot be produced at all.
invariant: T3 acceptance criterion: the full suite on Python 3.12 and 3.14, results per cell
root: guard enumerates its subject without exercising it

claim: The skill's frontmatter still says the base was handed over without a license, which LICENSE and NOTICE.md retired on 24.09.2026
scenario: A team runs `npx skills add mikey-semy/finetooth`; the installed SKILL.md is the file their reviewer reads and it states part of the kit has no licence, so the install is blocked or inventoried as 'licence unclear' — while LICENSE is plain MIT with both holders (verified identical to the skill's own LICENSE), NOTICE.md:20-27 records the 24.09.2026 grant and CHANGELOG.md:116-119 records the appendix as removed. The tests pin the skill's LICENSE file and version string, so nothing goes red on this field.
invariant: NOTICE.md/LICENSE as the repository's rights contract; the skill's licence statement must equal the root one

claim: NOTICE.md's unqualified promise that road-tested projects are not named is contradicted by CHANGELOG.md:40, which names the owner's own project and one of its paths
scenario: NOTICE.md:31 says the names of the projects the method was road-tested on, their internals and the defects found are not published; CHANGELOG.md:40 and CHANGELOG.ru.md:40 name `setfork H3` with the path `curation/adapter.ts`, and the path also sits in review.py:2636 and tests/test_review.py:788,794, shipped inside the skill. The project is the repository owner's own (every clone under Projects/setfork* has an origin of mikey-semy/…) and the paragraph's heading is 'Other people's projects', so no third party's data is disclosed — but the sentence as written is false, and the CHANGELOG is never deleted.
invariant: NOTICE.md anonymisation; the promise must be scoped to what the repository actually does

claim: The stated security boundary ('writes to docs/review/', 'sends nothing over the network') is false for `summary` and for assets/run-role.sh
scenario: Measured on a clean repository: setup, init, coverage and status wrote only under docs/review/, but `summary` with no arguments created docs/review-summary.md outside it (SUMMARY_DEFAULT at review.py:1271, written at 1417-1421) and `summary --out` wrote outside the repository entirely. By SECURITY.md:15's own definition that is a reportable vulnerability for intended behaviour, consuming the one-week triage window. Conversely run-role.sh:25 leaves the assembled prompt and the whole event stream in $TMPDIR/finetooth-runs, and :38 sends the prompt over the network via `claude -p`. SECURITY.md names none of the three.
invariant: Invariant 7 — only docs/review/ is written, plus what the user explicitly asked for (summary --out); a security promise must match the shipped behaviour

claim: README (en, ru) and AGENTS.md give the suite as 98 scenarios taking about a minute; measured, it is 248 tests in 201 seconds
scenario: A contributor follows AGENTS.md:68 'Check before committing' and the runner reports 248 tests in 3 min 21 s against the promised 98 in about a minute — they cannot tell whether the checkout, the command or the document is wrong. The count appears at README.md:281,438, README.ru.md:228,377 and AGENTS.md:68; the runtime at AGENTS.md:68 and CONTRIBUTING.md:65. The figure tracked reality at 0.1.0 (25), 0.3.0 (67) and 0.4.0 (76) and stopped being updated, and it is the README's public evidence for 'tests proven by mutation'.
invariant: AGENTS.md rule 4 / CONTRIBUTING: numbers come from measurement, not from the head
root: a number in a public document not checked against its source

claim: README (en, ru) states the coupling shared-node threshold as a fixed six blocks and the mass cutoff as the 95th percentile; the code derives both
scenario: Reproduced by execution on a 9-block fixture: the tool printed `hub = coupled with >= 3 blocks` (hub_blocks() = max(3, ceil(0.10*n_blocks)), review.py:965-978), moved the 5-partner file into shared nodes and reported `no cross-block pairs above the thresholds` — so a user who read 'a file coupled with six or more blocks' hunts for a seam the tool has already filtered away. The printed threshold is 3 up to 30 blocks, 6 only at 51-60, 7 from 61. The same run printed `Tukey's fence over 17 commits — fewer than 20, too few for a percentile`, not the 95th percentile the sentence names.
invariant: The README documents behaviour the tool no longer has — the constant it quotes was replaced in this same unreleased version
root: a number in a public document not checked against its source

claim: The Unreleased section contradicts itself: Added says a shared node is a file coupled with >= 6 blocks, Fixed says the threshold became a share with a floor of three
scenario: RELEASING gate 4 takes the release notes from this section verbatim, so a user updating reads two mutually exclusive rules for the same mechanism (CHANGELOG.md:68 against CHANGELOG.md:36, and identically in CHANGELOG.ru.md) and cannot tell which behaviour the version has; anyone reconstructing why `coupling` filtered a file has two rules to choose from. The code agrees with the Fixed entry: COUPLING_HUB_SHARE = 0.10 with COUPLING_HUB_FLOOR = 3.
invariant: A CHANGELOG entry describing a mechanism the same section has already changed
root: a number in a public document not checked against its source

claim: The proposal template sends contributors to docs/prior-art.md and asks for a ROADMAP direction number; both were moved to a private repository
scenario: An outside contributor opens a Change proposal. The 'How to close it' field points at docs/prior-art.md (`git ls-files docs` lists only docs/review/ after CHANGELOG.md:83 moved docs/ and ROADMAP.md to the private finetooth-hq) and the next field asks for a direction number that exists only in a repository they cannot read. They leave it empty or invent one, and the maintainer gets proposals that cannot be placed against the plan.
invariant: Live contributor-facing guidance must point at files the repository has

claim: Versions 0.5.1, 0.5.0 and 0.4.1 have no compare link in either CHANGELOG, though RELEASING gate 4 requires one before the tag
scenario: A user on 0.4.0 opens the CHANGELOG to see what the next three releases changed. Parsing both files: ten version headings, seven defined link references (Unreleased, 0.7.0, 0.6.0, 0.4.0, 0.3.0, 0.2.0, 0.1.0), so 0.5.1, 0.5.0 and 0.4.1 render as literal bracketed text in Keep a Changelog's format — the diffs for the releases that added the fix-reviewer role, the block proof kind and the depersonalisation of the templates are the ones a reader cannot reach. CHANGELOG.ru.md:572-578 has the identical gap.
invariant: RELEASING.md:31 gate 4 — the compare link is added before the tag

claim: RELEASING calls its gates 'all mechanical' when three of the four are human steps that nothing checks
scenario: A maintainer (or a second one added under CONTRIBUTING's write-access rule) reads 'Gates — all mechanical, all before the tag' and treats them as enforced, then tags a release whose CHANGELOG section is incomplete, whose compare link is missing and which no live project has run. Nothing fails: CI runs only gate 2 (tests + skills-ref validate), and RELEASING.md:56-59 itself says gate 3 cannot be automated. This already happened — 0.5.1, 0.5.0 and 0.4.1 shipped without their compare links.
invariant: A rule declared enforced with nothing enforcing it, in the file that defines what a version number means
root: a rule declared enforced with nothing enforcing it

claim: The DCO sign-off is mandatory and nothing verifies it: no workflow checks commits, only a self-reported PR checkbox
scenario: An outside contributor commits without `git commit -s`; .github tracks nine files and none is a DCO job, the only workflow running on pull requests (tests.yml) checks the suite and the skill format, the PR-template checkbox at .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:13 is read by nobody, CI goes green and the PR is merged. The claim 'Every commit is signed with Signed-off-by' becomes false with no artefact showing which commits are covered. The habit holds throughout the last 30 commits, so the gap is purely mechanical: the first unsigned commit arrives from outside.
invariant: A rule declared enforced with nothing enforcing it; the DCO is the project's stated licensing basis
root: a rule declared enforced with nothing enforcing it

claim: README.ru.md has no counterpart to README.md:28-52 — the six claims that separate the kit from PR-review bots, and the Language paragraph
scenario: A Russian-speaking user follows the [Русская версия] link at the top of README.md, the only entry point offered, and reads a document without 'What makes it different from PR-review bots': the coverage map that fails on an unowned file, mandatory hypothesis verdicts, fingerprints, the register in git, guards from the third recurrence, mutation-proven tests — none of it stated as a guarantee in Russian. Choosing between finetooth and a PR-review bot, they have no comparison to read. The four-roles substance is present in Russian (README.ru.md:45-48); the differentiator list and the Language paragraph are not.
invariant: The two languages must say the same thing about what the tool guarantees

claim: The README's 'What is inside' inventory is incomplete in both languages: 19 of 23 commands, no axes.py or run-role.sh, and none of the ten .ru.md templates
scenario: A user writes their project's make targets or audits what the skill installs from this block — the only place the repository enumerates itself. `--help` registers 23 subcommands; the list names 19 (README.md:421-423, README.ru.md:360-362), omitting `coupling`, `order`, `summary` and `refs`, and `refs` appears nowhere in either README at all, so it is never run. The same tree omits scripts/axes.py and assets/run-role.sh (the two files that write outside the repository), the ten .ru.md templates and assets the `lang` switch selects, and at root .gitignore, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.ru.md and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.ru.md.
invariant: A section whose purpose is to enumerate the kit must enumerate it

claim: The release procedure names two paths that do not exist: `scripts/review.py` and a root `SKILL.md`
scenario: A release follows step 2 literally and finds no scripts/review.py — `git ls-files` has no entry starting with scripts/ and no SKILL.md at the root; the files are skills/finetooth/scripts/review.py:60 and skills/finetooth/SKILL.md:7, the layout having moved in 0.4.0. Either the release stalls on a wrong document, or a new scripts/review.py is created while the real version strings stay at the old number, and the test pinning the skill header to VERSION then fails on the release PR for a reason the message does not explain.
invariant: A mandatory release step must name files the repository has

claim: actions/checkout is taken by the mutable tag v5 while every other action and install in the same two workflows is pinned by commit
scenario: The v5 tag is moved — a compromised publisher account or a breaking re-tag — and every push to master/dev and every pull request runs different code in the checkout step. A step that controls the working tree can make the suite pass, and since green CI is what branch protection requires before a merge into master, the gate reports green on a tree whose tests were never honestly run. stale.yml:19 pins actions/stale by digest and tests.yml:31 pins skills-ref to a commit, which CHANGELOG 0.4.0 records as deliberate. The job declares only contents: read and uses no secret, so a false-green check is the realistic worst case, not exfiltration.
invariant: The repository pins CI actions by commit; the exception guards the gate the release depends on

claim: The CI workflow's step names and comments are in Russian, against AGENTS.md rule 7 and the 0.7.0 English-primary release
scenario: An outside contributor's PR goes red: the GitHub checks panel names the failing step in Russian ('Настроить git', 'Прогнать тесты', 'Проверить формат скилла') and so do the comments explaining why each step exists, in a repository whose CONTRIBUTING.md:8 promises English for code and whose AGENTS.md:56 allows Russian only in the named .ru.md copies. Cyrillic elsewhere in the tree is deliberate (the MSG table, Russian test names and their quotation in the docs), so a workflow is the only reader-facing file that is Russian-only with no bilingual form.
invariant: AGENTS.md rule 7 — content in English, with Russian copies only as .ru.md files

claim: `init` answers a Python traceback on a blocks.json without the top-level review_id, and the guard test that forbids exactly that stays green
scenario: Measured: a hand-written blocks.json with a valid block but no top-level review_id, run through all 23 subcommands. Twenty-two behave (exit 2 naming the missing state file, or exit 0); `init` alone ends in KeyError: 'review_id' — a traceback and exit 1 — because check_definition (review.py:495-526) validates only the per-block fields. The guard HandWrittenInputTest.test_ни_одна_команда_не_роняет_трейсбек_на_битом_определении (tests/test_review.py:3059) asserts no command tracebacks on a broken definition, but its stand always writes review_id (tests/test_review.py:82), so the suite is green. README step 2 names only project and gates to fill in.
invariant: Invariant 12 — a traceback reaching the user is a defect; invariant 2 — a guard that can be holed with the suite green is not a guard; CHANGELOG.md:29,88 claim this class closed
root: hand-edited input reaches the code unvalidated

claim: SKILL.md states the tool is tested on Python 3.12 and 3.14, while the CI workflow pins no Python version and runs the suite on one
scenario: A team installs the skill into a repository whose CI image carries a different Python and relies on the compatibility line as tested ground. tests.yml has no actions/setup-python and no matrix: both steps call the runner's default python3, so exactly one version is ever exercised and which one moves with the ubuntu-latest image. No other public file states a Python requirement at all. The measured syntax floor is low (one `from __future__ import annotations`, no match statement, no tomllib, no datetime.UTC), so the risk is not that it breaks today but that nothing would catch it when it does.
invariant: A claim stated as verified with nothing verifying it — the same class as the DCO and the release gates
root: a rule declared enforced with nothing enforcing it

claim: Neither code of conduct links to its other-language copy, against the 0.7.0 claim that the Russian copies are cross-linked at the top of each file
scenario: Checked the first line of all six bilingual files: README.md and README.ru.md carry the link, CHANGELOG.md and CHANGELOG.ru.md carry it, both codes of conduct begin with a blank line and have no link in either direction — against CHANGELOG.md:100-103, which names CODE_OF_CONDUCT.ru.md among the copies 'cross-linked at the top of each file'. A Russian speaker landing on CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, the file GitHub surfaces in the community profile, has no way to discover that the translation exists, so a document that was made and committed goes unread.
invariant: The two languages are reachable from one another; a stated release claim must hold
